ceiling_statement: FROZEN GUARANTEE. The maximum feasible coordination under H1-H8 is DETERMINISTIC PARALLELISM WITH ATOMIC TIER COMMIT AT A SINGLE LOGICAL SERIALIZATION POINT: the committed result is bitwise equal to the unique canonical serial execution (fixed topological order with deterministic tie-break); concurrency is bounded by DETERMINISTIC CONFLICT-ORDERED EXECUTION — a pre-committed serialization order under which even NON-COMMUTING stages execute concurrently with deterministic outcome (Calvin-class deterministic concurrency control) — NOT by the commuting fraction of the effect algebra: disjoint-write-footprint antichain parallelism is the simplest admissible schedule, not the outer boundary; wall-clock speedup is bounded below by max(T_work/p, T_span) over the DAG's critical path (Brent's work-span law) for p declared workers; and all inter-agent arbitration is reduced to deterministic, data-defined admission at ONE LOGICAL SERIALIZATION POINT — a physical kernel-enforced single writer seat, or a machine-checked nonforking replicated total order — never to timing, races, or unaccountable votes. Any stage failure aborts its entire tier with the pre-tier state restored exactly.
derivation: Three limits compose, restated without the v1 errors. (1) Replay limit, corrected: H5 (deterministic replay) plus H8 (third-party recompute) require the committed output to be a function of frozen inputs alone; an execution whose result depends on physical interleaving is unreplayable. The boundary is DETERMINISM OF OUTCOME, which is achievable two ways: (i) commuting-effect antichains with a deterministic merge order (Church-Rosser confluence), and (ii) deterministic conflict-ordered execution — pre-committing a serialization order and executing non-commuting stages concurrently under mechanisms that guarantee the outcome equals that order's serial result. Route (ii) demonstrably admits MORE concurrency than the commutativity bound while remaining a pure function of frozen inputs, so the v1 claim 'no feasible system can admit more concurrency than the commuting fraction' is retracted; the ceiling is the deterministic-outcome frontier. (2) Scheduling limit: the work-span law T_p >= max(T_1/p, T_inf) is information-flow arithmetic on the DAG; under H6 speculative state may never become visible in the trusted store, so speculation can discard work but not beat the span bound. (3) Arbitration limit, with the FLP misuse struck: FLP bounds deterministic consensus in the fully asynchronous faulty model only; it caps neither a single-authority model (where no consensus is needed) nor partially-synchronous BFT total ordering (feasible and in production). The arbitration ceiling is a deterministic decidable admission predicate evaluated at the single logical serialization point; on a single-authority operating model, kernel-DAC enforcement below the code is the strongest available seat; on a multi-authority model, a machine-checked nonforking replicated total order is strictly stronger in operator-independence at declared consensus-resource cost. H3 forces failure semantics: a failed stage cannot be marked executed; the only fail-closed option is atomic tier abort with exact pre-tier state (ties to AX-11).
relativity_note: The choice between physical single-writer and replicated-total-order realizations of the serialization point is a declared-resource choice; the deterministic-outcome frontier itself is invariant across both.
lean_obligation: Given a finite DAG G over stages with pure per-stage semantics and declared footprints, and a pre-committed total serialization order ord: define exec_serial as the fold over ord and exec_conflict_ordered as concurrent execution constrained to produce ord's outcome. Prove: (T-confluence) for disjoint-footprint antichain scheduling, every valid schedule yields exec_serial's result; (T-conflict-ordered) exec_conflict_ordered equals exec_serial for ALL stage pairs including non-commuting ones — determinism from order pre-commitment, not from commutativity — with a witness schedule exceeding the antichain concurrency fraction; (T-abort) if any stage of tier k fails, execution returns the exact state after tier k-1; (T-span) makespan of any p-worker schedule >= max(totalWork/p, criticalPath G), and the greedy scheduler achieves <= totalWork/p + criticalPath G.

attainment_witness_appendix.candidate_mechanism: A deterministic tier-commit executor in SBCL: (a) tiers from the deterministic topological sort (pipeline-dsl.lisp + dependency-graph.lisp) with lexicographic tie-break; (b) tier stages as lparallel futures writing only to stage-private scratch directories; (c) tier commits only when every future succeeds — outputs merged in the fixed order and installed via the AX-11 atomic commit; any stage error discards the tier scratch and signals fail-closed; (d) writer-seat arbitration is the executionally-proven OS-DAC closure (identities.sh uid pinning; verify-capability-closure.sh real setpriv write attempts, BLOCKED-never-PASS); (e) candidate arbitration is the admission predicate of admission-model.sexp as a pure SBCL function. The Calvin-class conflict-ordered rung is a declared-resource upgrade beyond the scratch-and-merge scheme. POSIX + SBCL + lparallel.
attainment_witness_appendix.b0_gap_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: parallel-executor.lisp swallows per-stage errors (handler-case to nil, lines 71-81) and unconditionally marks failed stages executed (line 88) — no rollback, no tier abort — while stages mutate a shared context concurrently, making intra-tier order observable; the kernel-DAC arbitration seat is proven but not connected to the engine executor; no atomic tier commit or scratch-then-merge discipline exists. B0 has the arbitration half and lacks the deterministic-parallelism half; the conflict-ordered rung is absent entirely.
